description:
Today every package an external Go module would need to consume mosey as a library — `transport`, `transport/libp2p`, `transport/unix`, `transport/http2`, `auth`, `cert`, `vterm`, `attach`, `streambuf`, and `api` (for the protocol-ID constants) — lives under `mosey/internal/`. Go's `internal/` rule makes them unimportable from outside this module, so the relationship described in `docs/src/relationship-to-shepherd.md` ("shepherd consumes mosey as a library") is currently impossible: shepherd cannot `import "github.com/firefly-engineering/mosey/internal/transport"`.

This is a hard prerequisite for shepherd's planned rebase onto mosey (it blocks even adding mosey to shepherd's `go.mod` in a useful way).

Two plausible shapes:

1. **Move packages to module root or `pkg/`.** Direct, but ties the public Go API one-to-one to today's internal layout. Any rename later becomes a breaking change.
2. **Thin `pkg/` re-export wrappers.** Each public package re-exports the types/funcs shepherd needs (`pkg/transport` aliases `internal/transport.Transport`, `pkg/vterm` aliases `internal/vterm.Session`/`Run`/`Options`, etc.). Keeps the internal/ layout free to evolve.

Either way the minimum public surface for shepherd is:

- `transport`: `Transport`, `Stream`, `Handler`, `Multi`, `ErrUnsupported`/`ErrUnsupportedScheme`
- `transport/libp2p`: `New`, `Config` (incl. `Identity crypto.PrivKey`)
- `transport/unix`: `New`, `Options`, `Scheme`
- `auth`: `Wrap`, `Authenticator`, `Identity`, `IdentityOf`, the PSK + cert constructors
- `cert`: `NewMasterMnemonic`, `MasterFromMnemonic`, `MasterPublicKey`, `Sign`, `Verify`, `Claim`
- `vterm`: `Run`, `Options`, `Mode` constants
- `attach`: `Run`, `Options`
- `streambuf`: `OutputRing`, `InputQueue`, defaults + drop policies
- `api`: the `/mosey/...` protocol-ID constants

Once this lands the wire model and HKDF labels become a commitment, not an implementation detail — worth pinning the "changing them is a deliberate version bump" rule (already in AGENTS.md) into the public package doc too.
title: Lift consumed packages out of internal/ so external modules can import them
